leaving.title: Resigning and leaving
leaving.resign: Press “Resign” to give up; the app asks first before ending the game.
leaving.abandon: Online: if the player to move has not moved for 5 minutes, the other player can press “Claim the win” and win the game.
leaving.abandonRoom: Online: if the player to move has not moved for 5 minutes, the others can claim their turn abandoned.
leaving.standIn: In a room of 3–4: the computer plays for whoever resigned or left (“Played by the computer”) until the game ends; they play again from the next game. In a room of 2: the game ends and the other player wins.
leaving.vsAi: Against the computer: resigning means the computer wins.

goal.title: Goal
goal.body: Two players take turns marking X and O on a 3×3 board. The first to get three in a row wins.

moves.title: Moves
moves.body: X goes first. On your turn, place one mark on an empty square; a square already marked cannot be taken.

win.title: Winning
win.body: Three of your marks in one of the eight lines: 3 rows, 3 columns or 2 diagonals. The game ends at once, even when the winning move fills the last square.

draw.title: Draw
draw.body: All 9 squares are marked and nobody has three in a row: it’s a draw.

lines.label: Three 3×3 boards: three X in a row, three O in a column, three X on a diagonal
lines.caption: Three kinds of winning line: a row, a column, a diagonal.

goal.title: Goal
goal.body: Two players take turns marking X and O on a grid. The first to get 5 in a row across, down or diagonally wins; with the “Blocked ends” rule, that line must not be blocked by the opponent at both ends.

board.title: Board and turns
board.body: A 15×15 or 19×19 board, picked on the setup screen along with the winning rule. X goes first; on your turn, mark any empty square.

free.title: The “Free style” rule
free.body: Five or more in a row across, down or diagonally wins, whatever is at either end.

blocked.title: The “Blocked ends” rule (default)
blocked.body: As in free style, unless both squares just past the two ends of the line hold the opponent’s marks: then that line does not win. The edge of the board does not block. A line longer than 5 wins on the same condition.

draw.title: Draw
draw.body: The board is full and nobody has won: it’s a draw.

five.label: Five X in a row on a diagonal: X wins
five.caption: Five X in a row on a diagonal: <yes>X wins</yes>.

blocked.label: Top row: five X blocked by an O at both ends, no win. Bottom row: five X blocked at one end only, X wins
blocked.caption: Top: blocked at both ends, <no>no win</no>. Bottom: blocked at one end only, <yes>a win</yes>.

edge.label: Five X touching the edge of the board, an O at the other end: X wins, as the edge does not block
edge.caption: Touching the edge, an O at the other end: <yes>a win</yes>, as the edge does not block.

board.title: Board and track
board.body: 2–4 players, each with a colour and a symbol (Red ●, Blue ■, Yellow ▲, Green ◆) and 4 horses starting in the stable. A horse comes out on its colour’s start square, goes exactly once round the shared 56-square track in one direction to its home entry (the square just before the start square), then climbs the 6 home steps.

turn.title: Turns and rolling a 6
turn.body: On your turn, roll the die, then choose a horse that can move by that number; if none can, you lose the turn. Rolling a 6 gives you another roll after moving, even when no horse could move.

out.title: Bringing a horse out
out.body: Only with a 6, onto your colour’s start square. You cannot bring one out while one of your horses is on the start square; an opponent’s horse there is sent back to its stable.

move.title: Moving and sending home
move.item1: Move exactly as many squares as you rolled.
move.item2: Never jump over a horse, yours or an opponent’s.
move.item3: Never stop on a square holding one of your horses.
move.item4: Stopping right on an opponent’s horse sends it home to its stable.
move.item5: Never move past your own home entry: stop right on it before climbing home.

one.title: Rolling a 1: jump to a home entry
one.body: With a 1, a horse on the track jumps to the nearest home entry ahead (of any colour, even one nobody plays; at most as far as its own) if every square in between is empty and none of your horses is on it. If it can jump, it must, and an opponent’s horse on that home entry is sent home. If it cannot jump, it moves 1 square.

home.title: Climbing home
home.body: From your home entry, a roll of k goes straight to step k if steps 1 to k are all empty. From step n, you only climb to step n + 1 with exactly n + 1. At home, horses never pass each other and are never sent home.

win.title: Winning
win.body: The first player with all 4 horses on steps 3, 4, 5 and 6 of their home wins; the game ends at once.

path.label: The cross-shaped board: a Red horse comes out on its start square, goes once round clockwise to its home entry, then climbs home from step 1 to step 6
path.caption: Red’s way on the real board: start square (●), direction (arrows), home entry (ring) and home steps 1–6.

jump.label: Top row: a Red horse rolls a 1, the way is clear, it jumps to the next home entry and sends the Yellow horse there home. Bottom row: a Blue horse is in the way, the Red horse only moves 1 square
jump.caption: Top: the way is clear, <yes>it jumps to the home entry and sends Yellow home</yes>. Bottom: a horse in the way, it moves 1 square.

home.label: The 6 home steps: from the home entry a 4 goes straight to step 4; from step 4 it takes exactly a 5 to reach step 5
home.caption: A 4 from the home entry: step 4. From step 4: exactly a 5. Four horses on steps 3–6 win.

goal.title: Goal
goal.body: Checkmate the opponent’s king: it is in check and has no way out.

board.title: Board and turns
board.body: An 8×8 board, with the light square h1 in White’s right-hand corner. White moves first, then the players take turns. No move may leave your own king in check.

pieces.title: How the pieces move
pieces.queen: Queen: any number of squares along a row, a column or a diagonal.
pieces.rook: Rook: any number of squares along a row or a column.
pieces.bishop: Bishop: any number of squares along a diagonal.
pieces.knight: Knight: an L shape (two squares, then one to the side), jumping over other pieces.
pieces.pawn: Pawn: one square forward (two from its starting row), capturing one square diagonally forward.
pieces.capture: Except the knight, no piece passes over another. A piece captures by moving onto an opponent’s piece.

castling.title: Castling
castling.body: The king moves two squares towards a rook, and the rook jumps to the square on the king’s other side. Allowed when the king and that rook have never moved, the squares between them are empty, the king is not in check, and neither the square the king crosses nor the one it lands on is attacked.

enPassant.title: En passant
enPassant.body: An opponent’s pawn has just moved two squares and stopped right beside your pawn on the same row: your pawn may capture it by moving diagonally to the square it passed over. Only on the very next move.

promotion.title: Promotion
promotion.body: A pawn reaching the last row becomes a queen, rook, bishop or knight of its colour, chosen by the player.

end.title: End of the game
end.stalemate: Stalemate: the side to move is not in check but has no move: a draw.
end.automatic: Automatic draw: a position repeated for the fifth time, 75 moves by each side without a pawn move or a capture, or too little material to checkmate (such as two kings alone, or two kings and a knight).
end.claim: Claiming a draw: once a position has repeated three times, or after 50 moves by each side without a pawn move or a capture, the side to move gets a “Claim a draw” button that ends the game drawn at once, without the opponent’s agreement.

chess.credit: Pieces: the “staunty” set by sadsnake1 (Lichess), licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

moves.label: Six small boards, each with a piece in the middle and dots on the squares it can reach: king, queen, rook, bishop, knight, pawn
moves.caption: Where each piece can go (dots): king, queen, rook; bishop, knight, pawn.

castling.label: White castles kingside: before, the king on e1 and the rook on h1; after, the king on g1 and the rook on f1
castling.caption: Castling kingside: king e1 → g1, rook h1 → f1.

enPassant.label: En passant: a black pawn has just moved from d7 to d5, beside a white pawn on e5; the white pawn captures by moving to d6
enPassant.caption: Black has just played d7 → d5: the white pawn on e5 captures by moving to d6.

promotion.label: Promotion: a white pawn moves from e7 to e8 and becomes a queen, rook, bishop or knight, as chosen
promotion.caption: A pawn on the last row: choose a queen, rook, bishop or knight.

goal.title: Goal
goal.body: Get your pawn into its gate before anyone else. The gate is the 5 middle cells of the opposite edge, the third to the seventh column or row, drawn as a village gate in your colour and symbol.
goal.body2: The other cells of that edge do not count: a pawn there has to walk along the edge into the gate.

board.title: Board and fences
board.two: Two players: a board of 11 rows × 9 columns, 9 fences each.
board.three: Three players: a 9 × 9 board, 6 fences each.
board.four: Four players: a 9 × 9 board, 4 fences each.
board.body: Everyone has exactly one break. The first seat starts.

turn.title: One thing each turn
turn.body: On your turn, do one of three things: move your pawn one cell, place a fence, or break a fence.
turn.body2: A pawn moves along a row or a column, never through a fence. Pawns may share a cell and do not jump over each other.

place.title: Placing a fence
place.body: A fence is two cells long and lies on a line between cells. It may not overlap another fence, even in part, nor cross one at its middle.

way.title: A way to the gate, always
way.body: A fence may not leave anyone without a way to their gate, yourself included. Other pawns do not count as obstacles.

break.title: Breaking a fence
break.body: Everyone may break once a game, instead of moving or placing. You may break anyone's fence; a broken fence goes back to nobody.

end.title: End of the game
end.body: The first to step into a cell of their gate wins at once, with any number of players. Another player's gate does not count. After 200 moves in all (198 moves with three players) with nobody home, the shortest way wins; level ways draw.

gate.label: The top edge has a gate over its five middle cells. A pawn just outside it takes one step along the edge into it
gate.caption: The ● pawn is on the edge but outside the gate, so it has <no>not won yet</no>. One step along the edge into the gate wins.

place.label: Three small pictures: a fence on a line, a fence overlapping another, a fence crossing another
place.caption: A whole fence with round ends can go there. A fence broken in two with a ✕ <no>cannot</no>.

sealed.label: A pawn in the right corner has one way out, to the left; a fence on that way is forbidden as it would seal the pawn in
sealed.caption: The ■ pawn has one way out (the dots). The ✕ fence would <no>seal it in</no>, so it is forbidden.

break.label: Before breaking the fence the way is {before} steps; after it, {after} steps
break.caption: Breaking the ringed fence takes the way from {before} to {after} steps.
